description: The OpenSky Network is a crowdsourced network of ADS-B, Mode S, FLARM and other receivers that records aircraft surveillance messages worldwide and makes them available for research. Data products include a live and recent REST API of aircraft state vectors, the full historical database queried through Trino, curated scientific datasets (weekly 24-hour state-vector samples, raw data, the COVID-19 flight dataset, in-flight emergency and climbing aircraft datasets, an ADS-C dataset) and an aircraft metadata database downloadable as CSV in monthly snapshots. The network was initiated in 2012 by researchers from armasuisse Science and Technology and partner universities and is now a non-profit association in Switzerland; receivers are hosted by volunteers, companies and institutions. Coverage is global but best in Europe and the United States, with generally no data before 2013. Access: the REST API is for non-profit research and education, the Trino history is granted free to university researchers, governments and aviation authorities, and any for-profit use needs a written licence. Caveats: coverage gaps over oceans and sparse regions, and the metadata database is only updated irregularly. OpenSky trajectories feed network flow, capacity planning, resilience and emissions studies and are processed with the traffic library and OpenAP, the latter catalogued here.
